$comment: CRSF Phase 2Q (CR-VERIFY-003): canonical register of historical security fixes. Checked by security/crsf/lib/fix-register.mjs (test/fix-register.test.mjs). One invariant per fix; PROVEN = E4 (behavioural regression test + known-bad mutation expected KILLED and executed by security:verify).

discovery.note: patterns are defined in security/crsf/lib/fix-register.mjs; copied here for review only

tests.test: ^NPM-SIGNATURES b706956 check:ci verifies registry signatures with the real npm and fails on a tampered package$

fixes.evidence_note: real npm 11.17.0 `npm run check:ci` (network evidence, capability npm_network = CRSF_NETWORK_EVIDENCE=1): npm refreshes the Sigstore TUF metadata online from tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev and takes the registry keys from the TUF target registry.npmjs.org/keys.json; pacote verifies every dist.signatures entry against "<name>@<version>:<dist.integrity>". Positive: fresh disposable cache against the real registry passes. Known-bad: in a disposable copy of that cache only dist.integrity of one direct dependency (@vercel/analytics) is changed (real signature kept), read with prefer-offline while TUF still refreshes online: check:ci fails with "1 package has an invalid registry signature" for exactly that package. Network boundary (preload in every node process): only tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev and registry.npmjs.org, asserted; no credentials (empty user and global npmrc), nothing published or written to the registry. Not proven: a compromise of the registry signing key itself; attestation (provenance) verification is reported but not part of the invariant; without CRSF_NETWORK_EVIDENCE=1 the evidence is NOT_RUN.

fixes.evidence_note: real `vercel build` (local official build path, no deployment, npm offline) executes the installCommand of the repository vercel.json; with a lockfile that does not match package.json npm ci aborts the build and leaves the lockfile unchanged. Control with a matching lockfile builds. Known-bad without installCommand: Vercel's default npm install rewrites the lockfile and builds. Not proven: the hosted Vercel build container (runs the same CLI build logic; not observable locally); Vercel's second, function-level install (covered by .npmrc, 51c0cd4).

fixes.evidence_note: real Vercel CLI (installed version, capability vercel_cli) computes the upload set of `vercel deploy` for a seeded project with the repository .vercelignore and reports it to a local fake API that refuses the deployment; no network, no upload, no deployment. Control without the file: the same CLI would upload .env and .env.production (its defaults only ignore .env.local / .env.*.local). Not proven: Vercel Git-integration uploads (none: Git deployments are disabled, e3270c1).

commit_policy: Every historical commit up to 1.0-draft-phase2r is classified by hash above (all commits, not only keyword matches). Every later commit must carry exactly one trailer "Security-Fix: FIX-<id>[, FIX-<id>]" (registered fixes) or "Security-Fix: none - <reason>" (>= 10 characters); the guard fails on a commit with neither (full history and shallow clones; not asserted without git).
